text: Our checkout integration tests fail about 1 in 5 runs on CI. They pass locally. Anyone seen this?
Probably shared Postgres state. The suite runs four workers against the same schema, so two tests can create the same order at once.

I reproduced it. The failure is a duplicate key on orders_external_id_key because the retry creates a second order row. The CI token in the job is ghp_FAKEfakeFAKEfakeFAKEfake1234567890 and my email is priya.nair@acme.example if you need the logs.
So the retry isn't idempotent? That would explain why it only shows up under load.

Right. create_order() inserts before it checks the idempotency key. The fix is to make the insert ON CONFLICT (external_id) DO NOTHING RETURNING id, then select the existing row when no id comes back.
Also don't retry on IntegrityError. We should only retry on connection errors and 5xx responses. I added a test that calls the handler twice with the same key and asserts one row.
We decided to use a per-worker schema via the pytest-xdist worker_id and keep the idempotency fix. That isolates the DB and removes the shared-state race.
Gotcha: if you use --dist loadscope, all tests in a module share a worker, so schema setup has to be session-scoped or you will create it twice.
Verification: run pytest tests/integration -n 4 --count=3 and confirm zero duplicate-key failures. Also check pg_stat_activity has one schema per worker.
